security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU indirect CSR access handler for iselect=0x1000 (aclicsourcecfg base) makes the full sireg2/mireg2 register read-only zero instead of only enforcing read-only zero on bits [15:0]; OR fails to enforce read-only zero on bits [15:0] while exposing writable bits [31:16]
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: iselect dispatch table or xiselect_aia_range() not handling iselect ∈ [0x1000, 0x10FF] as aclicsourcecfg with per-index WARL masks; wr_mask unconditionally zeroing full dword at iselect==0x1000; missing per-bit WARL constraint that bits[15:0] are read-only zero only for k==0
security_spec.summary: sireg2 at iselect=0x1000 maps to aclicsourcecfg[0] where only bits[15:0] are read-only zero (sourcecfg[0]), while bits[31:16] are writable (sourcecfg[1]); full-register read-only-zero blocks legitimate sourcecfg[1] config causing function loss, while omitting the read-only-zero on bits[15:0] allows write to hardwired-zero sourcecfg[0] bypassing platform interrupt policy

findings.finding: When smcsrind/sscsrind ISAs are enabled, iselect writes are masked with ISELECT_MASK_SXCSRIND (0xfff). A guest write of 0x1000 has bit 12 masked off, silently collapsing to 0x000. This is correct per the Sxcsrind spec: 0x1000 is not a defined indirect-access select value, so no WARL register should preserve it. The guest's next sireg/sireg2 read gets the iselect=0x000 encoding, which raises ILLEGAL_INST via rmw_xireg_csrind.

iselect=0x1000 falls outside both the AIA IPRIO range [0x30,0x3f] and the IMSIC range [0x70,0xff], so xiselect_aia_range() correctly returns false. This prevents 0x1000 from being dispatched to rmw_xireg_aia, which would treat it as reserved (isel_reserved=true) and return ILLEGAL_INST. Correct behavior.

iselect=0x1000 matches neither xiselect_cd_range() (0x40-0x5f) nor xiselect_ctr_range() (0x200-0x2ff). Falls through to the else branch returning RISCV_EXCP_ILLEGAL_INST. No code path exists that would treat 0x1000 as aclicsourcecfg and expose sireg2/mireg2 with incorrect WARL masks. The illegal-instruction trap is the safe default for an unimplemented feature.

The top-level dispatch in rmw_xireg first checks xiselect_aia_range(). Since 0x1000 is not in AIA range, it falls through to the csrind branch (if smcsrind/sscsrind are present). rmw_xireg_csrind then rejects 0x1000 as unimplemented. No smidctrl-specific dispatch arm or ACLIC sourcecfg handler exists. No way for sireg2/mireg2 to be accessed with iselect=0x1000 and return data.

The Smidctrl extension and aclicsourcecfg indirect CSR registers (iselect ∈ [0x1000, 0x10FF]) are completely unimplemented in this QEMU tree. Zero references to 'smidctrl', 'SMIDCTRL', 'aclicsourcecfg', 'ext_smidctrl' exist in any source file or git commit. The PR referenced in the spec context ('Smidctrl: Correcting first element definition fo aclicsrccfg') has no corresponding code changes in this repository. The vulnerability pattern (sireg2/mireg2 with wrong WARL masks at iselect=0x1000) cannot manifest because the code path to reach those registers with that iselect value does not exist.
